extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing monographs for the American Mathematical Society using AMS-LATEX document classes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting AMS monographs using AMS-LATEX classes, covering file organization, preamble/package usage, top-matter tagging, math/theorem/equation conventions, graphics, floats, bibliographies, indexing, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplied template and appropriate document class
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for your particular publication and the appropriate document class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy the template to a suitably named file and specify the correct \documentclass (e.g., \documentclass{gsm-l} for Graduate Studies in Mathematics). Using the supplied template minimizes production work and errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful, limited file names
rubrics_metrics.description: File names should not exceed 20 characters and consist only of numeric or unaccented alphabetic (ASCII) characters. Avoid overly generic file names such as chap1.tex, mybib.tex or fig1.eps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give files meaningful names (e.g., grey-ch1.tex). If the author name is common, include initials to make it unique. This avoids confusion when files are transmitted to the AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions; page sizes must conform to the specifications of the publication for which you are preparing your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text width is determined by the trim size; changing it will change line breaks (especially for math displays) and cause production rework and possible errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change default font size (except for proofreading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify the default font size, except temporarily for proofreading your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing font size affects line breaks; if you do change size, reprocess your document before submitting and fix bad breaks. Obtain agreement with Acquisitions Editor for nonstandard sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public CTAN packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only 'public' packages available from CTAN (the Comprehensive TEX Archive Network).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not load unnecessary packages. The AMS document classes already load amsmath and amsthm functionality and usually amsfonts unless [noamsfonts] is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redeclare existing LaTeX/AMS commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeﬁne any existing LATEX or AMS-LATEX commands. Use \newcommand, not \def, to be warned if the name you have chosen is already in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redefining one-letter commands; remove any unused command definitions before submission. Redefinitions can cause mysterious errors in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put macros/definitions in the preamble and reuse consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Place definitions for frequently occurring mathematical expressions together in the preamble, before the start of the text of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a macro is created for an expression, use it for every occurrence of that expression. When the file is complete, remove any commands that haven’t been used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use author-defined macros in top matter or references
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use author-deﬁned macros in author names, titles, section and theorem headings, or references; use only standard commands. Do not hard-code font changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author-defined macros in top matter can break indexing and bibliographic services or make titles/bookmarks inaccurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid math in titles and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of math in the title and in chapter and section headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TEX math coding (especially dollar signs) will result in inaccurate bibliographic listings and problematic PDF bookmarks; only limited fonts are compatible in titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classiﬁcation numbers representing the primary and secondary subjects of the work and enter them with \subjclass[2020].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one primary classification is required. Use full MSC numbers from www.ams.org/msc. Omitting [2020] will cite the 1991 classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure graphics fit within margins and follow graphics guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that graphics do not extend into the margins; check that all graphics conform to the AMS graphics guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3 for file formats, resolution, color-space, line widths, type sizes, and other graphic requirements. Graphics that overflow margins cause production issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid explicit TeX line/page breaks and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use TEX coding to control line and page breaks or explicit horizontal/vertical spacing commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines/pages may break differently in the published book; hard breaks will likely be removed and could introduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbers on the left (AMS style)
rubrics_metrics.description: For displayed equations, the AMS style requires equation numbers to be on the left, flush with the left margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left numbers are default (equivalent to [leqno]). Right numbering ([reqno]) is supported but strongly discouraged because of incompatibility with proof-end \qed boxes. For multiline displays, options [centertags] or [tbtags] affect vertical placement of tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \cite for citations and provide full reference information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \cite to indicate citations in the manuscript and include all available information for references; use journal and series abbreviations from [ABMR].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic data will be converted to amsrefs form if not already in amsrefs, drawing data from MathSciNet when available (enhanced references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide author addresses and contact info in top matter (not inside \author)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the research address (required), current address (optional), email (optional), and URL (optional) for each author as separate tags (\address, \curraddr, \email, \urladdr). Do not include addresses within the scope of an \author{} command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses are part of top matter; do not use abbreviations; suitable labels will be added by the class. Email may appear online; URLs will not appear online but will in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread and verify source files match accepted copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your book thoroughly and carefully. Verify that author-submitted source files exactly match the accepted reference copy of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications in some series will not receive editorial proofreading. The files sent must be the EXACT files used to generate the accepted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a driver file and separate chapter files (use \include not \input)
rubrics_metrics.description: A monograph should use a driver file and put the source code for each chapter in a separate file, using \include (not \input) to assemble them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies structure and helps production. Front-matter data should be placed in the driver file.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS will add an AMS-specific hyperref later
rubrics_metrics.description: An AMS-specific version of the hyperref package will be added by AMS staff at the appropriate stage of the production process primarily for PDF bookmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may affect internal cross-references and external URLs; authors should not add conflicting hyperref setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters generally begin on right-hand (odd) pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, every chapter must begin on a new right-hand (odd-numbered) page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the default [openright] behavior unless otherwise agreed for short chapters; [openany] may be used for drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter and running-head capitalization and short titles
rubrics_metrics.description: In chapter titles, capitalize first and last words and all nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, and verbs; articles, conjunctions, and prepositions lowercased except first/last words. Provide a shortened form in brackets for running heads when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running heads on left-hand pages should have the chapter title (shortened only if needed); right-hand running heads should have the section title. Starred headings lack an optional short form; use \markboth or \markright to set running heads in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide grant and copyright metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Give information for grants or contracts (including grant numbers) under which the research was performed, in the preface; provide primary classification numbers and other required data for the copyright page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright/title pages are prepared by AMS from provided information. For translations include original publisher, year, and translator details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do preamble package loading and macro definitions there
rubrics_metrics.description: The area between \documentclass and \begin{document} is the preamble; load external packages and define document-specific commands there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all packages are compatible with AMS classes; see allowed/avoid lists. Put all new command definitions in the preamble and avoid redeﬁning existing commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document class options: paper size, oneside/twoside, draft/final, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate \documentclass options: paper size defaults to [letterpaper] (a4paper allowed for drafts), [twoside] default, [draft] or [final] versions, font sizes per series, [openright]/[openany], [leqno]/[reqno], [fleqn], [centertags] or [tbtags] for multiline tag placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft options mark overfull lines and show graphics bounding boxes. Changing default options affects line breaks and must be checked before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended compatible packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Several packages are compatible and recommended for use (amssymb, amsbooka, imakeidx, chngcntr, graphicx, longtable, mathrsfs, mathtools, natbib, upref, tikz, xypic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some appear in templates. Use packages only if needed and ensure compatibility with AMS production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packages to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain packages cause production problems and should be avoided: biblatex, epsfig, diagrams (Paul Taylor), geometry, microtype, makeidx (not needed), parskip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using unsupported packages will require conversion or manual fixes and may introduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define theorem environments in preamble using amsthm
rubrics_metrics.description: Activate theorem types in the preamble using \theoremstyle and \newtheorem. Three predefined theorem styles: plain (italic), definition (upright), remark (upright, no extra space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Numbering options: 
ewtheorem{thm}{Theorem} for global numbering, 
ewtheorem{thm}{Theorem}[section] to number within sections, and 
ewtheorem{lem}[thm]{Lemma} to number consecutively with another counter. Use amsthm facilities rather than the various LATEX theorem packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top matter tags and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided top-matter tags (e.g., \title, \author, \contrib, \address, \curraddr, \email, \urladdr, \dedicatory, \date, \thanks, \translator, \subjclass, \keywords, \maketitle). Some tags are required, others optional as listed in Table 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place top matter after \begin{document}. The template contains necessary tags and instructions. If no short form is needed, omit bracketed optional arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title formatting restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The book \title is for identification during production; avoid math in titles and use only compatible fonts (Computer Modern family, amsfonts with amssymb, mathrsfs script fonts) in titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final printed title page will be generated by AMS. Use \\ for desired manual line breaks if needed. Titles should be input in style appropriate for bibliographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributor tagging format
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors are tagged like authors but are responsible for portions of the document; use \contrib[exact printed text]{Name} where bracketed text is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple \contrib lines are combined with correct punctuation. Provide addresses for contributors similarly to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject classifications and keywords formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter subject classifications as \subjclass[2020]{Primary ...; Secondary ...} separated by commas; at least one primary classification is required. Key words may be provided with \keywords{...}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full MSC number. Only the first word and proper nouns are capitalized in keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagging for maximum web linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag the manuscript for maximum linking on the Web using \label, \ref, \cite, and \eqref where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS will add an AMS-specific hyperref. Use \eqref for equation refs (produces roman parentheses), and consider upref for roman internal refs in non-roman environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading levels and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the six heading levels provided (\part, \chapter, \specialsection, \section, \subsection, \subsubsection) and provide labels with \label{...} directly after headings for cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an optional short form in brackets for running heads when needed. For starred headings needing running heads, use \markboth or \markright. Run LATEX at least twice to resolve cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman type and math coding conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers, punctuation, parentheses, brackets, braces, and symbols used as labels should ideally be set in roman type even within italic theorem text. Mathematical expressions must be coded as math ($...$ or \\(...\\)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \textup{...} for roman text in non-roman environments; use control sequences for common functions (log, lim); use \DeclareMathOperator for new operator names. Use upref package if roman refs are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise environments for inline and end-of-chapter exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the xca environment for exercises appearing within a section; use the xcb environment for exercises at the end of a chapter (presented as a section with enumerated \item entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare these with \theoremstyle{definition} and \newtheorem in the preamble as per templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing with MakeIndex or imakeidx
rubrics_metrics.description: Include index terms directly in TEX files; use \makeindex in the preamble and \printindex where the index should appear. For multiple indexes use imakeidx with the [original] option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the makeidx package (classes include needed tags). Run MakeIndex separately and rerun LATEX to incorporate indexes. Use imakeidx syntax to declare and print additional indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float handling: numbering, placement, references, and section containment
rubrics_metrics.description: Floats should be numbered consistently (figures and tables separately), placed at top or bottom of page, have an in-text reference, and appear within the same section as their first text reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A figure/table should not precede its first text reference unless on the same page spread. Allow floats to float (avoid [h!] option). Production staff will determine final placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption location and labeling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions are usually positioned above a table and below a figure. Caption headings (e.g., 'Table 3.1.' or 'Figure 7.') are supplied automatically; the caption text may be omitted. Place \label after the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caption style differs from basic LATEX; LATEX caption packages may not match AMS style. Use the figure/table environment structures illustrated in the handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS classes auto-center floats; do not add \centering
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS classes center the content of table and figure environments; using \centering or \begin{center} is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant centering commands; plain figure/table content will be centered by the class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables must fit text width and caption above
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that the width of the table does not exceed the width of the text block. Set table captions above the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very wide tables can be rotated using the rotating package with the sidewaystable environment; rotate so the left-hand side of the rotated table is at the bottom of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics file formats and resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable formats include EPS, TIFF, JPEG for photographs and graphics; photographs must be at least 300 dpi at the actual printed size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TEX. Bitmap graphics must meet resolution requirements (see Chapter 3). For color photos use CMYK. For TEX-generated graphics prefer tikz/pstricks/xy; provide graphic code inline or in a dedicated file if lengthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics and color-space requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics intended to be printed in color should be submitted in CMYK format; RGB files will be converted to CMYK and reproduction is not guaranteed to match the RGB file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert color graphics to grayscale before submission if they will print in black-and-white; check grayscale output on a black-and-white printer to ensure legibility. Be aware of gamut differences between RGB and CMYK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colored lines, tints, and light colors handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Colored lines should be no less than .5 point in width. Colored lines in inherently light colors (e.g., yellow and cyan) should be at or near 100% tint. Inherently light colors should be handled carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 50% yellow or cyan may be almost invisible in print; check legibility and adjust tints accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type in graphics: minimum size and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic type size within graphics should be no less than 10 point at 100%. Do not put type on a dark background; check color figures on a black-and-white printer for legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10-point may be hard to read online due to low screen PPI; consider larger sizes for online viewing. Labels added by external labeling packages can extend outside graphics—check and add \vspace if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph file and color requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must be at a minimum resolution of 300 dpi at the actual size printed. File format can be EPS, TIFF, or JPEG. Color photographs must be saved in CMYK format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TEX. AMS will optimize color graphics for printed publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using TeX graphics packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tikz (PGF), pstricks, xy/xypic for TEX-generated graphics where appropriate. These are recommended for diagrams and charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikZ is flexible and works with dvips/pdfLaTeX/XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX. Provide large code inline only if short; otherwise place in a separate file and \input it. See referenced documentation and primers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use label-placement packages carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that place labels on graphics ensure consistent fonts but labels outside the graphic boundary can extend into margins or overprint surrounding material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check graphics carefully where external labeling is used; add \vspace if labels extend outside edges to avoid overprinting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare bibliographies with amsrefs or BibTeX (no biblatex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographies may be prepared using either amsrefs or BibTEX. Methods using other packages, including biblatex, are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not using amsrefs, AMS will convert bibliographic data to amsrefs drawing from MathSciNet where possible (enhanced references). Use \cite commands for citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit only needed files and bundle when multiple files
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance send only the files needed to process or archive the submission (TEX source and graphics). If multiple files, bundle them using Zip to reduce name conflicts and corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send .log or .aux files. Verify all checklist items before sending. The files sent must be the exact files used to generate the accepted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission channels and metadata in email
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred submission is via the AMS web server (www.ams.org/submit-book-journal) which requires an AMS web account. Email submissions are accepted at pub-submit@ams.org with attachments (not in message body) and the subject line should include the publication code and author name(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions via email will be auto-acknowledged; problems with files will be reported. For submission problems contact AMS Technical Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact AMS Technical Support and Acquisitions for help
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter difficulties preparing/submitting manuscript files, contact AMS Technical Support (tech-support@ams.org, phone numbers provided) or the Acquisitions Department (acquisitions@ams.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For web server problems contact webmaster@ams.org. The handbook lists telephone numbers and postal address for correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online and community resources for TeX support
rubrics_metrics.description: For TeX/LATEX assistance consult AMS TEX pages, CTAN, the TEX Users Group (TUG), the comp.text.tex Google group (CTT), and tex.stackexchange.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS is not equipped to handle platform-specific questions; use community resources and listed references for TeX help and package documentation.
